Indexing a scalar list needs a positional read of an array column, which Prisma's filter API cannot express. The refusal arrives one node earlier than p-index's, because there is no get-field projection wrapping this index

A positional read of a number list has no Prisma filter form: Prisma's scalar-list filters (has, hasSome, hasEvery, isEmpty, equals) test membership or the whole list, never one position, and exist only where the provider has array columns, which SQLite and MySQL do not. `index` has no case in the translator's operator switch, so the walk throws at the index node itself, before the list is resolved against the mapper or the element's type meets the literal — the same site as index-scalar-list

Cannot translate endsWith with a needle: A backslash is a LIKE metacharacter on some providers and not others, so the same needle cannot mean the same thing on all of them: SQLite's LIKE has no escape character and matches a backslash literally, while PostgreSQL and MySQL treat it as the DEFAULT escape character with no ESCAPE clause present. endsWith('\\') is then a pattern ending in an escape character, which PostgreSQL rejects outright (SQLSTATE 22025), and a backslash anywhere inside a needle silently escapes the next character so contains('a\\b') would match 'ab' — a row the PDP denies. Prisma emits no ESCAPE clause and cannot escape the backslash, so the adapter throws instead of filtering differently per provider

ne value type does not match mapped numb: The `!=` mirror of eq-number-vs-string: CEL answers `aNumber != "5"` TRUE for every row, and a store that coerced '5' = 5 would drop a1, an under-grant rather than an over-grant but a wrong filter all the same.
